title: Expression Evaluation and Safe Arithmetic
learningObjectives: Explain expression evaluation and safe arithmetic in C++.
Identify the operators, operands and result types involved.
Predict an expression's result by tracing it.
Use the topic in a focused program.
Avoid common mistakes and choose a clear alternative.

understand.concept: Safe expression design checks input ranges, types, conversion, division by zero, overflow risk and shift counts. Signed integer overflow is not guaranteed to wrap.
understand.whyItMatters: Accurate expression understanding prevents logic errors and improves safety, readability and maintainability.
understand.explain: Study expression evaluation and safe arithmetic through the rule summary and examples; trace values carefully and note type and edge-case constraints.

practise.guidedTask: Trace all five examples for expression evaluation and safe arithmetic. Predict the result first, then modify an operand and explain the change.
practise.independentTask: Create a short C++ program applying expression evaluation and safe arithmetic to a practical problem. Include three test cases and one boundary case, and explain your choices.

Use parentheses or separate statements to clarify intent.

questions.prompt: What is guaranteed for signed integer overflow?
options: It is not guaranteed to wrap; overflow can be undefined behavior
questions.answer: It is not guaranteed to wrap; overflow can be undefined behavior
questions.explanation: Signed overflow is not safely assumed.

questions.prompt: What should be checked before integer division?

Why can wider intermediate types help?
options: They may provide additional range for intermediate results
They make overflow impossible for every input
questions.answer: They may provide additional range for intermediate results
questions.explanation: Wider types can reduce risk, not eliminate it.
